tytul: Fresh white sausage, raw or simmered (UGA)
wstep: This card covers fresh white pork sausage, raw or simmered as a fresh sausage, using the safety rules of the UGA Extension sausage bulletin.

ostrzezenia.tekst: Fresh sausage is raw: keep it in the refrigerator and cook it thoroughly before eating.
UGA recommends cooking products made from ground pork and beef to an internal temperature of 160 °F.

akapity: JarAtlas rule (cautious): the UGA bulletin has fresh sausage recipes but none for white sausage, so this card gives no ingredients or spices, marjoram included, only the safety rules for fresh sausage.
Fresh sausage is made from ground meat mixed with seasonings, and it must be refrigerated and thoroughly cooked before eating.
Keep the meat and other ingredients refrigerated at 40 °F or below (about 4 °C), also while you work, and check with a thermometer.
If you will not cook the sausage right away, put it back in the refrigerator as soon as it is made.
UGA recommends cooking products made from ground pork and beef to an internal temperature of 160 °F, and poultry to 165 °F.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): however you cook it, cook fresh sausage until a thermometer shows 160 °F (about 71 °C) inside.
According to the FDA, color and texture are unreliable signs of safety, and a food thermometer is the only way to be sure.
A temperature of 144 °F is considered lethal to all trichinae.
According to UGA Extension, fresh sausage keeps 7–10 days in the refrigerator at 35–40 °F, or 4–6 months in the freezer.
NCHFP gives a shorter limit for raw red meat: keep it at 40 °F (about 4 °C) or below and use it within 3–5 days, or freeze it.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): use raw fresh sausage within 3 days, the shortest of these limits, or freeze it.
JarAtlas rule (cautious): throw away raw fresh sausage that has been in the refrigerator for more than 3 days.
Do not keep sausage out of the refrigerator for more than 2 hours, or for more than 1 hour when the temperature is above 90 °F (about 32 °C).
